title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as on the neighbouring pages. K is a field finitely generated over Q, Γ = Gal(K̄/K), and U is a hyperbolic curve over K. π = π_1(U_K̄) is the geometric fundamental group, and Ũ is the universal pro-étale cover. X' = Û is Ũ completed by its points at infinity (cusps). Each cusp corresponds to an inertia subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1) of π, up to conjugation. A splitting of 1→π→π_1(U)→Γ→1 gives an action of Γ on X' compatible with the π-action. 'Conj. B' is a form of the section conjecture: such an action has a fixed point, either at finite distance (coming from a point x∈U(K)) or at infinity (a cusp, i.e. some L_i normalised by Γ). The previous page restated this as: π^Γ = 1, plus uniqueness statements. Those include that the L_i normalised by Γ is unique, which is a weakening of the conjecture L_i = Cen π^{Γ^0}.

On this page Γ^0 is the subgroup acting trivially on roots of unity, Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞)). This is forced by the argument: Γ^0 must act trivially on L_i ≅ Ẑ(1).

Grothendieck strengthens Conj. B: Γ^0 (restricted from the given Γ-action) has exactly one fixed point on X'. Uniqueness forces that point to be Γ-fixed, since Γ^0 is normal in Γ.

Consequences, obtained by a clean fixed-point argument. Let g∈π centralise Γ^0. Then g maps the unique Γ^0-fixed point to a Γ^0-fixed point, so g fixes it.
- If the point is at finite distance, π acts freely on Ũ, so g = 1. Hence π^{Γ^0} = 1, i.e. the centraliser of Γ^0 in π is trivial.
- If the point is a cusp, g ∈ Stab = Norm_π(L_i) = L_i. This uses that cusp inertia groups are self-normalising, indeed malnormal, in surface groups. Hence π^{Γ^0} ⊂ L_i. Conversely, Γ^0 acts on L_i ≅ Ẑ(1) through the cyclotomic character, so trivially, giving L_i ⊂ π^{Γ^0}. This yields the 'highly plausible' relation π^{Γ^0} = L_i stated earlier.

He then asks whether these statements should hold for actions of Γ^0 alone, or of any group containing an open subgroup of Γ^0, without assuming they extend to Γ. On the next page he rephrases this: the whole theory should hold for K finitely generated over a cyclotomic field such as Q(μ_∞), not necessarily finite over Q. He also introduces 'Poincaré curves' (universal covers of algebraic curves up to commensurability) and their completions as the natural objects.
errors: The argument from uniqueness of the Γ^0-fixed point to π^{Γ^0}=1 or π^{Γ^0}=L_i is correct, granting freeness of π on Ũ and self-normalisation of the L_i.

The speculative generalisation at the end, to Γ^0-actions alone (i.e. a section conjecture over fields finitely generated over Q(μ_∞)), is very probably false as stated. The field Q(μ_∞), and fields finitely generated over it of transcendence degree 0, have cohomological dimension 1, so Γ^0 is projective. Sections of π_1(U_{K(μ∞)})→Γ^0 then always exist. Moreover, twisting by Hom_cont(Γ^0, π^ab-type quotients), which is uncountable because Γ^0^ab has infinite rank, should produce uncountably many π-conjugacy classes. Yet there are only countably many rational points and cusps over K(μ_∞), so 'each section has a fixed point' cannot hold. The version where the Γ^0-action is restricted from a Γ-action is not affected by this objection.

Even for restricted actions, uniqueness of the Γ^0-fixed point needs injectivity of points ↦ sections over K(μ_∞). This is a Kummer-injectivity statement for the Jacobian over K(μ_∞), requiring no nontrivial divisible points. It is plausible but is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Strengthened section conjecture: restricting a Galois section to Γ^0 = Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞)), the induced action on the cusp-completed universal cover has a unique fixed point
ideas.modern_name: section conjecture with uniqueness for restriction to the cyclotomic kernel (a 'Γ^0-rigidity' of sections)
ideas.usually_credited_to: section conjecture: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); restriction/uniqueness variants studied by Nakamura, Stix, Hoshi and others (unsure for this exact form)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 has the section conjecture; this Γ^0 strengthening is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Centraliser of Γ^0 in π is trivial (section from a rational point) or equals the inertia group L_i (cuspidal section)
ideas.modern_name: centraliser / Galois-rigidity statements for the outer Galois action on π_1 of hyperbolic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (Galois rigidity, centralisers of Galois images, 1990s); Hoshi–Mochizuki

ideas.what: Self-normalising (malnormal) property of cusp inertia subgroups used to identify the stabiliser of a cusp
ideas.modern_name: malnormality of cuspidal inertia in profinite surface groups

ideas.what: Proposal that anabelian / section statements hold over fields finitely generated over Q(μ_∞), only Γ^0 being needed
ideas.modern_name: anabelian geometry over Q^cyc / Q^ab-type fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: later work on anabelian geometry over infinite algebraic extensions (e.g. Pop and others; unsure)

missed.claim: A precise conjecture: for a section s of π_1(U)→G_K, the restriction s|Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞)) has a unique fixed point on the cusp-completed universal cover. Equivalently, the centraliser in π of s(Γ^0) is trivial or a cuspidal inertia group, with cuspidal sections recovered as L_i = π^{Γ^0}. This deduction of centraliser statements from uniqueness of fixed points of the cyclotomic kernel is a clean formulation not commonly stated.
missed.quote: je conjecture que dans la conj. B, il est même vrai que Γ^0 agissant sur X'=Û a un pt fixe et un seul
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a testable strengthening of the section conjecture, comparable with known centraliser results (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki), and isolates the cyclotomic kernel as the relevant subgroup.

missed.claim: The page links Grothendieck's hope to drop Γ to Γ^0 (fields over Q(μ_∞)) with the cohomological dimension 1 of Q(μ_∞) and Shafarevich's freeness conjecture for Gal(Q̄/Q^ab). These imply that the Γ^0-only version fails massively, with uncountably many sections. Only the 'restricted from Γ' version can survive.
missed.quote: si ces énoncés ne devraient pas être valables sans partir d'une action de Γ tout entier, mais seulement de Γ^0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It delineates which fields are 'anabelian enough' for section-type statements, a question still discussed (sub-p-adic fields vs Q^ab-type fields).

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a neat and correct derivation of centraliser statements (π^{Γ^0}=1 or L_i) from a uniqueness strengthening of the section conjecture for the cyclotomic kernel. These are close to later Galois-rigidity work but not clearly formulated in this form by Grothendieck in print. The speculative extension to fields over Q(μ_∞) is likely false in its strong form.
transcription_corrections: The relation is written 'π^{Γ^0} ⊂ Norm_π(L_i) = L_i' (inclusion sign, subscript π under Norm).
'd'où [?] la relation' is probably 'donc la relation'.
'{+fixe+}' is an interlinear insertion above 'point'; the sentence reads '(ce qui est plus fort, que ce point fixe soit nécessairement fixe par Γ)'.
